44120001.title: Show HN: Tinyqueue – a SQLite-backed job queue in 400 lines
44120001.summary:
Tinyqueue is a dependency-light job queue that stores everything in a single SQLite file, using a polling loop and row-level locking instead of Redis or a separate broker.

The author argues most apps never outgrow this, and walks through retries, visibility timeouts, and exactly-once delivery in under 400 lines.

On HN, commenters mostly agreed for small-to-medium workloads but pushed back on SQLite write contention under high concurrency, several recommending it only below a few hundred jobs per second.

44120002.title: The unreasonable effectiveness of plain-text logs
44120002.summary: The author makes the case that grep-able plain-text logs beat heavyweight observability stacks for most teams, citing lower cost and zero lock-in. HN's reaction was split: ops folks defended structured logging for high-cardinality queries, while smaller shops largely agreed text is underrated.

44120003.title: Ask HN: How do you stay current without burning out?
44120003.summary: The poster asks how engineers keep up with new tools without constant fatigue. Top replies favored ignoring most hype, going deep on fundamentals, and learning new things only when a real project demands it; several warned that chasing every framework is a fast path to burnout.

44120004.title: Apple announces the M5 MacBook Pro lineup
44120004.summary: Apple unveiled the M5 MacBook Pro, with the discussion centering on a reported jump in GPU cores and on-device model performance. HN was skeptical of the marketing benchmarks and debated whether the base RAM finally moved off 16GB.

44120005.title: A deep dive into CRDTs for collaborative editing
44120005.summary: An illustrated explainer of conflict-free replicated data types and how they power real-time collaboration without a central server. Commenters debated CRDTs versus operational transforms, with a few noting the memory overhead of tombstones in long-lived documents.

44120006.title: Why we moved off Kubernetes
44120006.summary: An engineering team explains migrating from Kubernetes to a handful of VMs and systemd units, citing operational complexity and cost. HN was characteristically divided — some called it a maturity-mismatch story, others cheered the simplification.

44120007.title: Rust's "async" & <Pin> — a beginner's guide
44120007.summary: A gentle introduction to why Rust's async functions need Pin<&mut T>, explaining self-referential futures and the <Unpin> escape hatch with minimal jargon. The piece uses a "don't move me" analogy that HN readers praised, though a few argued the borrow checker still makes async Rust harder than Go's goroutines.

44120008.title: PostgreSQL 19 beta 1 released
44120008.summary: The first beta of PostgreSQL 19 is out, headlining faster parallel vacuum and improved JSON indexing. The lone early comment flagged the new logical replication features as the most consequential for upgrades.

44120009.title: A small CSS trick for better focus rings
44120009.summary: A short tip using :focus-visible plus outline-offset to get accessible, good-looking focus rings without JavaScript. HN appreciated the simplicity, though some pushed for respecting forced-colors mode too.

44120010.title: Live: SpaceX Starship flight 12
44120010.summary: A live thread following Starship's twelfth integrated flight test. Commenters tracked the ascent and booster catch attempt in real time, debating reusability economics versus the program's pace of rapid iteration.

44120011.title: Understanding the Linux page cache
44120011.summary: A clear walkthrough of how the Linux page cache buffers file I/O, when pages are evicted, and how to read the numbers in /proc/meminfo. HN added war stories about misreading "free" memory and tuning dirty-writeback thresholds in production.

44120012.title: An oral history of the demoscene
44120012.summary:
A long feature tracing the demoscene from 1980s cracking intros to today's 64-kilobyte showcases, told through interviews with veteran coders and artists.

It highlights how brutal size limits bred extreme creativity in procedural graphics and sound synthesis.

HN readers shared nostalgia and links to favorite demos, with a side-thread on whether modern GPUs have made the size constraint more art than engineering.

44120013.title: Postgres vs. MySQL in 2026: a fresh benchmark
44120013.summary: A new benchmark suite finds Postgres 19 edging out MySQL 9 on complex analytical queries while MySQL keeps a slight lead on simple primary-key reads. Commenters cautioned that the workload favored Postgres and asked for the raw config, a recurring complaint about vendor-adjacent benchmarks.

44120014.title: The end of the password era
44120014.summary: A feature on passkeys finally reaching mainstream adoption across major platforms in 2026. Commenters welcomed the security gains but raised account-recovery and vendor-lock-in concerns when passkeys live in a single ecosystem.

44120015.title: Tell HN: I open-sourced my note-taking app after 5 years
44120015.summary: After five years as a paid product, the author released their note-taking app under MIT. The thread mixed congratulations with practical questions about sustaining maintenance and whether open-sourcing would cannibalize the hosted plan.
